content: Nicorette is a branded, over-the-counter treatment designed to alleviate the withdrawal symptoms associated with quitting smoking. It was originally part of Pfizer Consumer Healthcare Products Company but was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2006. Initially introduced as a transdermal patch for topical application, Nicorette later became available in other forms, including nicotine gum (made with nicotine polacrilex), lozenges, inhalers, and nasal sprays. All these products contain nicotine as their active ingredient and function by delivering nicotine into the bloodstream. These treatments are collectively referred to as nicotine replacement therapies (NRTs). Alternative brand names for Nicorette include Prostep, Habitrol, Nicotrol, Nicoderm, and Commit. Commit lozenges are specifically designed as an oral aid to help individuals quit smoking. They are available in two dosages: 4 mg, intended for individuals who smoke their first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking, and 2 mg, for those who wait more than 30 minutes before their first cigarette of the day. The lozenges, which are mint-flavored, are meant to be taken orally at least nine times per day during the first two weeks after a person decides to quit using tobacco products. Nicorette inhalers are also widely available over the counter in many regions. However, in the United States, they are marketed under the brand name Nicotrol Inhalers and are only available with a prescription. It is generally recommended to discontinue the use of Nicorette products after 12 weeks, as prolonged use or misuse can lead to nicotine dependence, similar to smoking. For those seeking more affordable options, online searches may reveal international or Canadian retailers offering Nicorette products at significantly reduced prices for U.S. consumers. Nicorette gum is available in several flavors, including: Original Mint Fruit Chill Fresh Mint
